name: Civette Green
lede: Civette Green is a dark yellowish green recorded by Ridgway in 1912, filed by the ISCC-NBS in 1955, and matched today to the industrial RAL 6011.

sections.title: Ridgway to RAL
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* gives this hue on plate XVIII, hue 31 minutes, tone k [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary lists the same color, first recorded in 1905, and the ISCC-NBS 1955 report files it as a dark yellowish green [2][3]. The name likely points to *civet*, the small carnivore whose coat runs toward this muted olive-green, though none of the sources we checked states this directly, so the link is undocumented here [2].

The modern industrial palette RAL lists a near-duplicate, RAL 6011, about 2 units away [4]. The nearest named colors on file are [[hay-s-green]], [[slate-green]], [[american-green]] and [[hay-s-green]], at 2.9, 4.1, 4.2 and 4.6 ΔE [5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: ColorHub's archive finds this color in 186 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [6]. It peaks in the 1930s, in 5 of 69 paintings, with a lift of more than nine times the archive's average rate for that decade [6]. Harald Giersing, Georges Seurat, Vincent van Gogh and Paul Cezanne each carry it more than most painters in the set [6]. The count is a computed match on photographed, varnished paint, not a pigment identification [6].
